name: TileDB
listed_description: Fast Dense and Sparse Multidimensional Array DBMS.
reason: No number against HDF5 or Parquet could be reached. The repo README, the 1.3.0 introduction.rst and the espg/TileDB fork README make only qualitative comparisons (HDF5 mostly dense, TileDB dense and sparse). TileDB-Inc/tiledb-benchmarks (archived) only compares against Zarr and bcolz, with no numbers in the reachable page. The VLDB 2017 paper 'The TileDB Array Data Storage Manager', whose abstract (search snippet only) says comparable to HDF5 for dense arrays and much faster random writes, is on blocked hosts (vldb.org, csail.mit.edu, academia.edu, aminer, springer), so its tables were not read. The only numeric third-party datum found is TileDB-Py issue #346, where one user wrote a 200,000 x 784 array in 11.7 s with TileDB versus 5.66 s with PyTables (HDF5), i.e. slower. The gist qiuwei/e1118d19692412a94f53abdb0536c441 has parquet-to-TileDB timing code but no results. Retry the paper from a host that allows vldb.org: it would give a tier B record (peer reviewed, versus HDF5 dense and sparse).
